items.proposed_content: The approximation error splits into two geometrically different mechanisms: coupling a frozen phase block to a Gaussian block is controlled by block-vector discrepancy, while freezing phases within a block is controlled by the relative spread of its primes. Smoothness of the total error requires both mechanisms to satisfy their own summability conditions.

items.proposed_content: The global functional limit closes through a nested approximation triangle. Fourier samples at logarithms of integers define the test norm; matched full, mixed, and truncated two-point kernels turn omitted spectral mass into fixed-test L2 truncation control; Fourier probing lifts this to negative-Sobolev and Wasserstein control; finite prime-phase equidistribution identifies each randomized truncation; and a Hilbert-valued martingale supplies the infinite randomized product before the final triangle inequality is applied.

items.proposed_content: For this dependent complex chaos, the real-imaginary cross-covariance produces a Cauchy-type two-point singularity whose phase and one-sided analytic spectral structure permit cancellation. Paley-Wiener boundary values and the Plemelj/Hilbert-transform estimate supply uniform L2 control, which in turn supports construction of the chaos as a negative-Sobolev-valued martingale.

items.proposed_content: The randomized Euler-product logarithm is decomposed into a singular first-prime harmonic and remainders that converge smoothly: higher prime powers are summable, block freezing and Gaussian coupling errors are smooth with exponential derivative control, and successive regularization of prime locations and Gaussian coefficients reaches a Brownian spectral field. Exponentiation therefore leaves the singular Gaussian chaos multiplied by an almost surely smooth nonvanishing arithmetic factor.

items.proposed_content: Fixed-window critical-line shifts do not acquire a continuous-function limit; after weight regularization they converge in law in weighted W^{-α,2}, for α>1/2, to a randomized-zeta boundary distribution. Its factorization as a smooth nonvanishing multiplier times complex chaos constructs the limit, while radial blow-up of the first prime harmonic, with higher harmonics bounded, contradicts the finite radial limits forced by any local measure representation.

items.proposed_content: The CUE argument reproduces the zeta-side approximation architecture with model-specific inputs: a finite trace exponential is the common truncation, Toeplitz/Fisher-Hartwig and strong Szegő asymptotics control its distance from the full characteristic polynomial, fixed traces converge to independent complex Gaussians, a Hilbert-valued martingale gives the global chaos limit, and dilation followed by Brownian coupling identifies the same mesoscopic chaos component used for zeta.

items.proposed_content: The paper's generalized-function limit needs only matched shifted second moments, which it proves through divisor-sum asymptotics, the functional equation, and uniform kernel estimates. Constructing real chaos directly from actual zeta would instead require the correct absolute-moment normalization and precise multipoint correlations; extending the picture to imaginary log zeta faces the additional dependence on zero locations.

items.proposed_content: Mesoscopic dilation separates spatial structure from a divergent scalar mode: randomized zeta factors into a smooth multiplier tending to one, a scalar complex Gaussian term with growing variance plus an order-one remainder, and a strict log-chaos distribution whose law is independent of the dilation. Passing to generalized functions modulo nonzero scalars removes the zero mode, leaving the same chaos law that also appears in the source's CUE mesoscopic theorem.

items.proposed_content: For normalized absolute powers of randomized zeta, the prime Gaussian covariance has one-half logarithmic singularity plus a smooth remainder. In the subcritical range, Gaussian-chaos uniform integrability and exponential control of the smooth coupling error transfer a nontrivial chaos measure; at and above the threshold the unrenormalized measure vanishes, while a critical normalization is transferred through covariance comparison and a convergent continuous factor.
